segments.t: In the kitchen, Artyom plates his gratin for Eleonora, but when Chef Barinov and Lyova taste it, the dish is terribly oversalted. Refusing to admit to Eleonora that he hired an incompetent cook, Viktor tells Artyom he has potential and secretly remakes the meal himself.
Можно подумать, у тебя с первого раза получилось.
Но чтобы не было вопросов, лучше я приготовлю сам.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'You can take an apron over there.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'apron' and 'may' in a few short words.
'The gratin! Right now I will bring the quail.' Denis anchors the line on 'gratin', while 'quail' completes the thought.
'Well, how is it?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'how'. Lyova answers right away.
'He handled it great!' The meaning hinges on 'perfectly' working together with 'handled it' in spoken Russian.
Можно подумать, у тебя с первого раза получилось.
'One might think you got it right the first time.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
'Well, how is the gratin?' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'gratin' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Not bad for the first time.' Notice how Russian expresses 'for' and 'not bad' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'It is clear that there is potential.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'one can see' before landing on 'potential'.
Но чтобы не было вопросов, лучше я приготовлю сам.
'But so there are no questions, I had better cook it myself.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'was' to negate the statement.
'And you rest for now.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'you' in a few short words.
'Thank you, Viktor Petrovich.' The grammar packs 'thank you' and 'proper name' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Why are you defending him, chef?' Lyova anchors the line on 'why', while 'proper name' completes the thought. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Можно подумать, у тебя с первого раза получилось.

That brings the kitchen tasting to a close. Notice how Chef Barinov softens his criticism and decides to cook the dishes himself to save face. See you next time!
